DataPropertyAssertion.Literal: Control ontology for the DL corner cases (consistency tests). Each expectation derived from the DL semantics. . Note: usesOntology is a relative file name in the same directory. Run configurations (kt:usesTestRunConfig) and reasoner configurations (kt:usesTestSystemConfig) may be assigned to the suite and apply to all of its tests.
Per test: ClassAssertion(ConsistencyTest) + task + usesOntology + expectedResult
A data max cardinality of one on xsd:dateTimeStamp is consistent with a single value of the datatype.
Two distinct xsd:dateTimeStamp values violate a data max cardinality of one.
An existential restriction whose successor is an inverse-at-most witness: satisfying it requires merging the named individual with another successor, which the saturation must not decide on its own.
The same contradiction behind a class definition (the asserted concept does not reveal it).
Margherita is subsumed by VegetarianPizza through the all-values restriction.

Issue #19: three pigeons on two holes force one hole to hold two pigeons, so the scene of that hole is a CrowdedScene and Scene is subsumed by CrowdedScene. This is the classifier's own test concept (Scene and not CrowdedScene) and it must be unsatisfiable.

Negative control for the pigeonhole case: the scene itself is a CrowdedScene, so (Scene and CrowdedScene) must stay satisfiable. A fix for the missing subsumption must not make this class unsatisfiable.

Issue #19, reduced variant from the issue discussion: one hole, two pigeons and the redundant axiom CrowdedHole subsumed by Hole. Removing that axiom makes the answer correct, so it belongs to the reproduction; the test concept must be unsatisfiable.
Negative control for the reduced pigeonhole variant: (Scene and CrowdedScene) must stay satisfiable.

Issue #19 as an ABox test: the ontology entails CrowdedScene(s), so asserting its negation must make the knowledge base inconsistent. This case passes and guards the ABox path while the cached subsumption test is repaired.
Issue #19 as reported: the classification must place Scene and CrowdedScene in one equivalence class (and TestSceneNotCrowded under owl:Nothing).
Issue #19, reduced variant: Scene and CrowdedScene must be classified as equivalent.

Nominal merge edge case: Node is the nominal {n}, k is an r-predecessor of n and a Forbidden, so (Node and (inverse r only (not Forbidden))) is inconsistent. The universal restriction is expanded on the test node before the merge with the nominal moves the link of k onto it, so the merge has to apply the restriction to the moved neighbour as well.

Negative control for the nominal merge edge case: the same universal restriction with the compatible filler Marker must stay satisfiable, so a fix for the missing application to the merged neighbours must not over-constrain them.

The existential counterpart of the nominal merge edge case: (Node and (inverse r some Forbidden)) is satisfiable and, because k is an r-predecessor of n, equivalent to Node, so the entailment Node is subsumed by (inverse r some Forbidden) is checked by the classification test of the same ontology.

Classification of the nominal merge edge case: TestForallMerge must be placed under owl:Nothing, TestForallMergeOk under Node, and Node and TestExistsMerge must be equivalent (the merge moves the predecessor link of k onto the nominal).

Completion graph caching, issue #19 variant (the holes are linked to the scene by role assertions): (Scene and not CrowdedScene) is unsatisfiable. The test merges the scene nominal into the test node, so the nodes that the cached model merged into the holes have to be rebuilt (criteria C8 and C11).
Control for the issue #19 variant (the holes are linked to the scene by role assertions): (Scene and CrowdedScene) is satisfiable.

Classification of the issue #19 variant (the holes are linked to the scene by role assertions): runs many satisfiability tests on the same cached completion graph, Scene and CrowdedScene are equivalent.

Completion graph caching, issue #19 variant (four pigeons on three holes, so three merged hole successors per model): (Scene and not CrowdedScene) is unsatisfiable. The test merges the scene nominal into the test node, so the nodes that the cached model merged into the holes have to be rebuilt (criteria C8 and C11).
Control for the issue #19 variant (four pigeons on three holes, so three merged hole successors per model): (Scene and CrowdedScene) is satisfiable.

Classification of the issue #19 variant (four pigeons on three holes, so three merged hole successors per model): runs many satisfiability tests on the same cached completion graph, Scene and CrowdedScene are equivalent.

Completion graph caching, issue #19 variant (negative control, two pigeons on two holes need not share a hole): (Scene and not CrowdedScene) is satisfiable. The rebuilt part of the cached model must not produce a clash that the knowledge base does not entail.
Control for the issue #19 variant (negative control, two pigeons on two holes need not share a hole): (Scene and CrowdedScene) is satisfiable.

Classification of the issue #19 variant (negative control, two pigeons on two holes need not share a hole): runs many satisfiability tests on the same cached completion graph, Scene is not subsumed by CrowdedScene.
Control: a pigeon that sits at the not crowded nominal h can be the pigeon a that already sits there.
Control: the individual a sitting at h is already entailed.
A second pigeon, different from a, at the nominal h that has at most one pigeon sitting at it (written as not (>= 2 inverse(sitsAt).Pigeon)) is unsatisfiable.
The pigeon b (different from a) cannot sit at the nominal h that has at most one pigeon sitting at it.

The nominal h1 has at most one Pigeon sitsAt-predecessor and the pigeon a sits at h1 by a role assertion; a test that adds the different pigeon b at h1 is unsatisfiable. Needs the at-most re-application on the new link (the saturation must not consume the dynamic reapply entries of the cached graph) and the C4 check of the cached h1 for neighbours that are new in the test or only expanded from the backend cache.
As before, but the pigeon d sits at h2 by (sitsAt value h2)(d), so the existing link is part of the cached graph and the new one comes from the test node.

An unqualified at-most restriction (at most two sitsAt-predecessors) on the nominal h3 with two asserted predecessors; the third one added by the test is unsatisfiable. C4 has to count new neighbours for unqualified restrictions as well.
Control: a non-pigeon at h1 does not count for the qualified at-most restriction, so it stays satisfiable.

Hub (the nominal {a} with an inverse r-predecessor in B) is not below Single (at most one inverse s-predecessor in F and an inverse r-predecessor in B). The classification test of Hub and not Single creates two distinct inverse s-predecessors in F as successors of the nominal. Their saturated expansion has to come from the saturated node of F, not from the node of the complement of F, which exists because Guard mentions the complement of F; otherwise the successors clash and Hub is wrongly placed below Single.

Control for the polarity of the saturated filler of at-least successors: the same filler F is used by an at-least restriction directly (Many, HubMany). HubMany is below Many and Hub, Hub is not below Many.

Classification with a nominal that is merged into a new empty node: T0 = (some inverse r0.{a1}) and ..., a1 is in C3 and C3 is below (=1 r0.C0) with C0 = {a2, a3} and r0 functional, so the test node of T0 is merged with a2 or a3 (T0 below C0, C4 below C3). The merge creates a new empty node of the nominal type; it received the merging hash and the backend cache data of the nominal but not the nominal individual, and the backend cache synchronisation dereferenced the missing individual (segmentation fault, reduced from fuzz seed 3241). Expected taxonomy from HermiT.

Classification with a nominal that is its own role successor: C2 = {a0}, C2(a1) and r1(a0, a1) make a0 its own r1-successor, and C2 below (=2 r1.C4) qualifies it. The two qualification branches of the at-most restriction localized a0 and then the successor, which is a0 again; the second local copy replaced the first one in the branch, the at-most merging continued on the replaced copy and never saw the link to the node it merged into, and the classification with completion graph caching did not terminate (reduced from fuzz seed 3016). Expected taxonomy from HermiT.

Classification in which a successor recorded as distinct by an at-most restriction is pruned because the node that created it is merged away: C1 = {a0, a1}, C1 below (=1 r2.C2), C2 below (all r0.C1) and C2 below (=1 r0.C2). The repair of the distinct nodes replaced a missing id by the node it was merged into, which for a pruned node is the node itself, so the id without a link stayed in the set and the classification with completion graph caching did not terminate (reduced from fuzz seed 3310). A pruned successor is now removed from the distinct nodes. Expected taxonomy from HermiT.

Classification in which a nominal is merged into the test node by a choice: C4 = {a0, a1}, r1(a0, a1), not-C2(a1), T2 = not-C4 and (at most 1 inverse r0.C2), T5 = not-C0 and (some inverse r2.C1) and (all r1.C2) and (at most 1 r1.C1). T5 is not below T2 (a1 can be in T5 and is in C4). The test of T5 and not-T2 merged a0 into the test node by the choice C4 = {a0, a1}; the backend cache synchronisation of the node visited its new individual a0 with the deterministic base dependency instead of the dependency of the merge, the expanded role assertion r1(a0, a1) carried no dependency on the choice, the clash with not-C2(a1) skipped the alternative a1 and the classification derived T5 below T2 (reduced from fuzz seed 2029). Expected taxonomy from HermiT.

Classification of a subsumption that only holds through nominals: C1 = {a2, a0}, C4 = {a4, a3}, C3 and C0 disjoint, C0(a0), C4(a0), C3(a4) and T2 = not-C3 and C4 and not-{a1}, so a0 = a3 and T2 is below C1. The model of T2 merges the test node with a3 = a0 and contains C1 without the internal consequences that C1 has in its own test; the pseudo-model pretest of the classifier took the missing consequence as proof of a non-subsumption and dropped the possible subsumer C1 without a test (reduced from fuzz seed 3208). The pretest now draws no conclusion when the model of the subsumed class contains the subsumer itself. Expected taxonomy from HermiT.

Classification in which two distinct at-least successors are merged through nominals by a functional role: C0 = {a1, a2}, C0 below (some inverse r1.C1) and C2, (some r0.C1) below C0, r1 below r0, r0 functional, C1(a0), C0(a0), T4 = (at most 1 inverse r0.C1) and {a0} and (all r0.C2), T5 = {a0} and (at most 1 r1.C2), so T5 is below T4. The two distinct r0-predecessors of the test of T5 and not-T4 were merged with a1 and a2 and the functional r0 merged these nodes; the mergeability check read the distinct edges of an older version of one node (the opposite node of a link), which did not have the edge yet, so the test answered satisfiable (reduced from fuzz seed 3203). isIndividualNodesMergeable now reads the distinct edges of the newest version. Expected taxonomy from HermiT.

Classification with a role assertion to a nominal that was merged into the test node by a choice: C1 = {a4, a1}, (some r1.C1) below C1, C1 below (=1 r0.C3), C0 below (at least 2 r1.C1), r0 functional, r0(a3, a1), C0(a3). C0 is not below C3 (a4 can be an instance of C0 outside C3). The test of C0 and not-C3 merged a1 into the test node by the choice C1 = {a4, a1}; the backend cache expansion of a3 linked its asserted r0-successor a1 to that node without the dependency of the merge, because the node already had a1 as its individual, so the clash of the functional r0 skipped the alternative a4 and the classification derived C0 below C3 (reduced from fuzz seed 2056, which answered differently from run to run). Expected taxonomy from HermiT.

NN-rule: D starts an r-chain of C-nodes that cannot close (r is inverse functional, all r-successors are not D), every C-node is an s-predecessor of the nominal a, and a has at most 5 s-predecessors (old OWLlink test 56-SIOQ-5). Was answered satisfiable: the anonymous chain was blocked before the at-most restriction of the backend-cached nominal was applied.
NN-rule: an asymmetric r2-chain closes only through at least three C2-nodes, each one an s-predecessor of the nominal b with at most 2 s-predecessors (old OWLlink test 55-SIOQ).
Control: the r3-chain can close in one node (an r3-loop), so b has one s-predecessor.
Control: r4 is inverse functional, but the start node can be its own r4-successor.
Classification of the NN-rule chains: D, C2 (and the tests equivalent to them) are unsatisfiable, the controls are not.

Two p-successors that are both the nominal a (forall p.{a}, at least 2 p): the saturation represents them by the shared top node plus an extension node with {a} and did not flag the clash (fuzz seed 2792).
Qualified variant (at least 2 q.A): was already answered correctly.
Inverse variant (forall inverse(t).{a}, at least 2 inverse(t)), the shape of fuzz seed 2792.
Control: one u-successor can be a.
Control: two v-successors can be a and b.
